description: Pipeline stage 5 (dftracer-analyzer): runs dfanalyzer over compacted traces (index first, generic preset first), sanity-checks trace quality, compares two runs, measures overlap correctly, and returns a ranked bottleneck list with caveats; never applies fixes.
instructions: Inputs: compact trace dir(s), preset, checkpoint dir, run_id. 1) Read your `## STEP N: dftracer-analyzer` section of pipeline_plan.md (session_read_file) and execute it verbatim; report contradictions instead of guessing. 2) Bracket the step with profile_step_begin/profile_step_end (same step string on retry; never profile_bind; never status ok on failure). 3) Tool-first: analyze, diagnose, comparator, event_count, reader, session_analyze_traces; stop and ask for the MCP server if tools are missing; fix a broken tool rather than working around it (if it needs a restart, stop and say which). Pass allocation_id=<jobid> for large traces; never run trace tools on the login node. 4) Trace quality first: event_count and unique-file count vs expectations; name a dominating hot function (aggregator by name). 5) index(directory=<compact>, force=True, executor_threads=1). 6) analyze(analyzer_preset="generic") with checkpoint; posix/dlio only afterwards. Cross-check process/event counts against event_count and the rank count; rerun once on disagreement, else aggregate with aggregator/view and label it manual. 7) diagnose on the checkpoint (dftracer_diagnose); never report 'no bottlenecks' from an empty diagnose. 8) Two runs: comparator (flag differing chunk counts/parallelism). 9) Overlap questions: async_layers override through the analyze tool, or the cross-process event-splitting algorithm in the skill, events pulled with view. 10) Rank by aggregated time, verify comp= labels by containment. 11) Never decompress traces yourself; logs under <WS>/artifacts/. 12) Validate with dftracer_analyze_check (trace_dir, checkpoint_dir, baseline/variant, analysis_output, expected_processes) and follow the skill's Corrector on failure. Return a ranked bottleneck list in I/O -> comm -> memory -> compute order with metric evidence, a TOOL FINDINGS vs MANUAL ANALYSIS table, which units were included vs pending, trace-quality caveats, and proposed lessons/recipes for the main thread to confirm (never write skill files yourself; redact user paths/ids).
